findings.problem: On any day carrying three or more moments, the received plan silently deletes the date line from the middle rows. A crowded row's plate paints an opaque 12px spread halo (box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px var(--back)), which is not part of its own box and so paints over the previously-painted sibling. A stacked LEAD is protected because b.css:332 gives it padding-bottom: var(--gap-snug); a stacked FOLLOW gets padding-top only, so its mono date sits flush with the plate's bottom edge, inside the band the next plate's halo covers. Driven at 390 and 1440, on ?v=paper and ?v=ink, on the owner plan and through Preview (what the guest gets): pull four moments back with the editor's own -7 stepper until three land on 25 July and two on 1 Aug, and the followers measure dateBottom == copyBottom (slack 0px) while every lead measures 12px, and 'Sat 25 Jul' renders as its top ~5px of glyph and nothing else - a title that looks complete over a date sliced through the x-height. Identical on both grounds, so it is not an ink-ladder split. Neither gate sees it: interaction-check asserts 'a stacked pair does not overlap on the render that forms it' and a PAIR is safe (the last follower has nothing painted after it), and 'no silent text clipping' looks for hidden overflow, not for an opaque shadow spread painting over a neighbour. This is the paid-for 'silent content deletion' class returning on the one surface the company is judged by, in the exact case a wedding guarantees - the ceremony, the photographs and the dinner on one date.
findings.fix: In b.css, give the follower the bottom padding the lead already has: change .b-item[data-stack="follow"] .b-copy (line 328) to { border-top: 1px solid var(--fore-16); padding-top: var(--gap-snug); padding-bottom: var(--gap-snug); }. Applied at runtime this restores every follower's date on both grounds (measured slack 0px -> 12px on all three followers, dates fully painted) with no other change to the composition; the stack's push arithmetic derives from measured heights and reflows on its own. Then add one gate assertion that a stack of THREE keeps every date painted - the existing pair assertion cannot catch it.

biggestWin: The rail is a scale, not a list, and it is drawn to scale in both directions. Sixteen days of nothing between 'Today, 16 July' and 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' are rendered as sixteen days of literal empty paper, so the answer to the only question the audience actually has - do I need to do anything yet - is felt before it is read, and 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' merely confirms it. The same instrument then reverses on the wedding morning: open Behind you and the column becomes DAYS BACK with 'We said yes' sitting 274 down. The owner's +7 stepper walks a row physically down that scale with the gap opening under it, animated because position is the quantity being changed. One idea, stated once, carried from the empty project to the printed sheet and holding on paper and at night. That is the memorable moment, and it is worth paying for.
